chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to wear the dyed (saffron-colored) and the radiant (bright) clothes.

key_terms.الْمُعَصْفَرَ: al-mu'asfar — clothes dyed with 'usfur (safflower), producing a yellow-orange or reddish-orange color
key_terms.الْمُنَيَّرَ: al-munayar — bright, radiant, or lustrous clothing; possibly referring to garments with a sheen or made from fine fabric

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Baqir wear saffron-colored and bright clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith records the personal dress practice of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him), the fifth Imam, as witnessed and reported by his companion Abu al-Jarud. The Imam wore mu'asfar (clothes dyed with safflower/saffron, producing yellow-orange hues) and munayar (bright or lustrous garments). This narration establishes a precedent in Islamic jurisprudence regarding the permissibility of wearing colored — particularly yellow/saffron-dyed — and visually striking clothing, a topic of some scholarly debate.
